description:
## Why
`for _ <- 1..3 do IO.inspect(:x) end` fails: parse/expected-token: unexpected item without a newline: Underscore. So do `IO.inspect not true` (Not) and `IO.inspect ~s(hi)` (Sigil("s")); Elixir runs all three. `for _x <- ...` and `{_, b} <- ...` parse. Found in fixture 01115's oracle twin.

The cause: `Parser::starts_no_parens_arg` (src/compiler2/frontdoor.rs) is a hand list of tokens that may begin a no-parens argument, a second answer to the question `parse_prefix` (same file) already answers. It lacks Underscore, Not and Sigil, which parse_prefix accepts.

## What changes
One answer to "may this token begin an expression": the no-parens argument test reads the same token set parse_prefix accepts. The only exception is the spacing rule that tells unary from binary `-`/`+`.

## Signal
A new oracle fixture (01381) runs `for _ <- 1..3`, `IO.inspect not true` and `IO.inspect ~s(hi)` and matches Elixir on all three paths. Related but distinct: fz-sc8.91.
title: A no-parens call argument starts with any token an expression starts with
